headline: Meriden school crossing guard killed in Broad Street crash
dek: The guard was struck shortly before 9 a.m. near Olive Street; the driver stayed at the scene as police began a reconstruction investigation.
body: A Meriden school crossing guard was killed Wednesday morning after being struck by a vehicle on Broad Street, a fatal crash that left the city mourning a familiar presence around one of its elementary schools. The [City of Meriden’s announcement](https://www.meridenct.gov/announcements/city-mourns-death-of-crossing-guard-struck-by-vehicle/) said police responded just before 9 a.m. to the collision, while [NBC Connecticut reported](https://www.nbcconnecticut.com/news/local/pedestrian-hospitalized-after-being-struck-by-vehicle-in-meriden/3784813/) that the crash occurred near 391 Broad St. and Olive Street.

Police, firefighters and emergency medical personnel began life-saving measures at the scene, according to NBC Connecticut. The crossing guard was taken to MidState Medical Center, where the person was pronounced dead. The city’s public statement did not identify the victim, and the news report said the person’s name had not been released while officials contacted relatives.

The driver remained at the scene, NBC Connecticut reported. That fact describes what happened immediately after the crash, not the outcome of the investigation: police had not announced charges or a finding about fault in the reports available Wednesday. The Meriden Police Traffic Crash Reconstruction Unit is handling the case, and investigators were asking anyone who witnessed the collision or has relevant information to contact the department.

Broad Street was closed between Olive Street and Charles Street while investigators examined the scene, according to NBC Connecticut. The closure created a morning traffic disruption for people moving through the corridor while police documented the roadway and investigated the crash. Officials had not announced when the full area would reopen in the initial reports.

The crash occurred near Israel Putnam Elementary School. Meriden Mayor Kevin Scarpati told NBC Connecticut that, to the city’s knowledge, no children were present at the time. That detail does not lessen the loss of the crossing guard, but it distinguishes the known circumstances from what might otherwise be assumed about a school-area crash. The mayor said counseling would be available to students, families and staff who need it.

The school district also expressed condolences and described the crossing guard as someone whose friendly presence and positive approach mattered to students and families, according to NBC Connecticut. The district’s response points to the role crossing guards play beyond directing traffic: they are part of the daily safety routine that connects children, families and school staff at the street level. The available reports did not say how long the victim had served in the position.

The city’s brief announcement offered no details about the vehicle, the driver, the victim’s identity or the conditions that preceded the impact. Those questions remain for the reconstruction investigation. The absence of charges in the first reports should not be read as a final conclusion about responsibility while police continue to establish what happened.

For Meriden, the next public milestones are the victim’s identification when relatives have been notified, any release of additional crash facts and the police reconstruction unit’s findings. Until then, the confirmed account is limited: a crossing guard was struck and killed just before 9 a.m. on Broad Street, the driver remained at the scene, and the city and school community are responding to the loss while investigators work to establish what happened.
location: Broad Street near Olive Street, Meriden, Connecticut
author: NorthEast News Desk
